daily_precip_records.name: daily_precip_records
daily_precip_records.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- station identifier: combine stn and wban when available to preserve uniqueness
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(stn, '') = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN COALESCE(wban, '') = '' THEN stn
    ELSE CONCAT(stn, '-', wban)
  END AS station_id,
  -- observation date assembled from year, month, day
  SAFE.PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(year, '-', LPAD(mo,2,'0'), '-', LPAD(da,2,'0'))) AS obs_date,
  -- precipitation value: keep as-is here; sentinel 99.99 should be normalized downstream
  prcp AS precip
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
WHERE prcp IS NOT NULL
daily_precip_records.description: Daily precipitation records (one row per station-day) with precipitation value and date, filtered to rows that have non-null precipitation values; do not apply year or threshold filters here. Also normalize any sentinel values into NULLs in a later normalization step (e.g., 99.99).

rochester_daily_raw.name: rochester_daily_raw
rochester_daily_raw.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- date (use obs_date from daily_2019_raw)
  d.obs_date AS date,

  -- temperature: convert Fahrenheit (daily_2019_raw.temperature) to Celsius
  -- lift literal conversion factor out: (temperature - 32) * 5/9
  CASE
    WHEN d.temperature IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN d.temperature = 9999.9 THEN NULL
    ELSE (d.temperature - 32.0) * 5.0 / 9.0
  END AS temperature_c,

  -- precipitation: use GSOD prcp from wildcarded noaa_gsod.gsod* tables.
  -- Convert inches to centimeters: inches * 2.54
  -- We join on station id composed of stn||'-'||wban to match station_id in daily_2019_raw if necessary.
  -- To keep view reusable and lift date range literals out, this view selects all dates but caller can filter.
  NULLIF(
    CASE
      WHEN g.prcp IS NULL THEN NULL
      WHEN g.prcp = 99.99 THEN NULL
      ELSE g.prcp * 2.54
    END,
    NULL
  ) AS precipitation_cm,

  -- wind speed: use gsod wdsp (mean wind speed in knots) converted to meters/sec
  -- knots to m/s: 1 knot = 0.514444 m/s
  CASE
    WHEN g.wdsp IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(g.wdsp AS FLOAT64) = 999.9 THEN NULL
    ELSE SAFE_CAST(g.wdsp AS FLOAT64) * 0.514444
  END AS wind_speed_ms,

  -- station id: prefer station_id from daily_2019_raw if present; otherwise construct from gsod stn/wban
  COALESCE(d.station_id, CONCAT(g.stn, '-', g.wban)) AS station_id

FROM
  -- primary daily source for 2019 (lifted as dependency)
  `daily_2019_raw` d

LEFT JOIN
  -- join to GSOD wildcard tables to bring precipitation and wind for the same date and station.
  -- Use wildcard across all years; callers should filter _TABLE_SUFFIX if they want a narrower range.
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*` g
ON
  -- match date components: gsod has year/mo/da as strings; daily_2019_raw.obs_date is DATE
  SAFE_CAST(g.year AS INT64) = EXTRACT(YEAR FROM d.obs_date)
  AND SAFE_CAST(g.mo AS INT64) = EXTRACT(MONTH FROM d.obs_date)
  AND SAFE_CAST(g.da AS INT64) = EXTRACT(DAY FROM d.obs_date)
  -- match station: gsod stn and wban vs daily station_id (allow both forms)
  AND (
    d.station_id IS NOT NULL AND (
      d.station_id = CONCAT(g.stn, '-', g.wban)
      OR d.station_id = g.stn
      OR d.station_id = g.wban
    )
    OR d.station_id IS NULL
  )
rochester_daily_raw.description: Select daily weather observations (temperature, precipitation, wind speed) for Rochester for the full date range that includes Jan 1–Mar 31 2019. Keep one row per station-day or location-day observation and include the date and raw measured values.

rochester_daily_clean.name: rochester_daily_clean
rochester_daily_clean.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical date in DATE type constructed from year/mo/da; keep as key
  PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(CAST(year AS STRING), '-', LPAD(CAST(mo AS STRING),2,'0'), '-', LPAD(CAST(da AS STRING),2,'0'))) AS date,

  -- normalize temperature: GSOD temp is in Fahrenheit with 9999.9 = missing
  -- convert to Celsius; mask missing/invalid values to NULL
  CASE
    WHEN temp IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN temp = 9999.9 THEN NULL
    ELSE (temp - 32.0) * 5.0/9.0
  END AS temperature_c,

  -- normalize precipitation: GSOD prcp is in inches with 99.99 = missing; convert to centimeters (1 inch = 2.54 cm)
  CASE
    WHEN prcp IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN prcp = 99.99 THEN NULL
    ELSE prcp * 2.54
  END AS precipitation_cm,

  -- normalize wind: wdsp is mean wind speed in knots (string per schema), missing=999.9
  -- convert to meters/second (1 knot = 0.514444 m/s)
  CASE
    WHEN wdsp IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) = 999.9 THEN NULL
    ELSE SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) * 0.514444
  END AS wind_speed_ms,

  -- station identifier: combine stn and wban when available to keep uniqueness and joinability
  -- preserve original parts so view remains joinable: use "stn-wban" when wban present, otherwise stn
  CASE
    WHEN wban IS NULL OR wban = '' THEN stn
    ELSE CONCAT(stn, '-', wban)
  END AS station_id

FROM
  -- query across all yearly shards; consumer of the view should filter with _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1929' AND '2024' as needed
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
rochester_daily_clean.description: Normalize and clean the raw daily observations: ensure numeric types, convert units if needed to Celsius (temperature), centimeters (precipitation), and meters/second (wind), and handle/mask invalid or missing values consistently.

rochester_daily_mavg8.name: rochester_daily_mavg8
rochester_daily_mavg8.body_sql:
SELECT
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', CONCAT(year, LPAD(mo,2,'0'), LPAD(da,2,'0'))) AS date,
  CONCAT(stn, '-', wban) AS station_id,
  -- mean temperature in dataset is in degrees F to tenths; convert to Celsius
  -- lift literal for missing value (9999.9) out of view consumers
  CASE WHEN temp = @missing_temp_f OR temp IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE (temp - 32.0) * 5.0/9.0 END AS mavg_temperature_c,
  -- precipitation is in inches; convert to centimeters (1 inch = 2.54 cm)
  CASE WHEN prcp = @missing_prcp_in OR prcp IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE prcp * 2.54 END AS mavg_precipitation_cm,
  -- wind speed fields (wdsp, mxpsd) are strings in some shards; use wdsp where numeric, convert knots to m/s (1 knot = 0.514444 m/s)
  CASE
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) = @missing_wdsp_kn OR wdsp IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) * 0.514444
  END AS mavg_wind_speed_ms
FROM (
  SELECT
    stn, wban, year, mo, da, temp, prcp, wdsp,
    -- compute 8-day moving averages per station ordered by date
    AVG(NULLIF(CASE WHEN temp = @missing_temp_f THEN NULL ELSE (temp - 32.0) * 5.0/9.0 END, NULL)) OVER (
      PARTITION BY CONCAT(stn,'-',wban)
      ORDER BY PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', CONCAT(year, LPAD(mo,2,'0'), LPAD(da,2,'0')))
      ROWS BETWEEN 7 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS mavg_temperature_c,
    AVG(NULLIF(CASE WHEN prcp = @missing_prcp_in THEN NULL ELSE prcp * 2.54 END, NULL)) OVER (
      PARTITION BY CONCAT(stn,'-',wban)
      ORDER BY PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', CONCAT(year, LPAD(mo,2,'0'), LPAD(da,2,'0')))
      ROWS BETWEEN 7 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS mavg_precipitation_cm,
    AVG(NULLIF(
      CASE
        WHEN SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) IS NULL THEN NULL
        WHEN SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) = @missing_wdsp_kn THEN NULL
        ELSE SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64) * 0.514444
      END, NULL
    )) OVER (
      PARTITION BY CONCAT(stn,'-',wban)
      ORDER BY PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', CONCAT(year, LPAD(mo,2,'0'), LPAD(da,2,'0')))
      ROWS BETWEEN 7 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS mavg_wind_speed_ms
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
  WHERE
    _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN @year_start AND @year_end
)
rochester_daily_mavg8.description: Compute the 8-day moving average (current day and previous 7 days) for temperature, precipitation, and wind speed for each station/date using an ordered window by date.

users_2021.name: users_2021
users_2021.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS user_id,
  creation_date AS creation_timestamp
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users`
WHERE
  creation_date >= TIMESTAMP("2021-01-01 00:00:00")
  AND creation_date <= TIMESTAMP("2021-12-31 23:59:59")
users_2021.description: All users whose account creation timestamp falls within the inclusive 2021 date range (2021-01-01 00:00:00 through 2021-12-31 23:59:59). Keep creation timestamp and user id for later joins.

questions_in_30d.name: questions_in_30d
questions_in_30d.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.id AS user_id,
  q.id AS question_id,
  q.creation_date AS question_creation_timestamp
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users` AS u
ON
  q.owner_user_id = u.id
WHERE
  q.creation_date >= u.creation_date
  AND q.creation_date <= TIMESTAMP_ADD(u.creation_date, INTERVAL 30 DAY)
questions_in_30d.description: All question posts whose creation timestamp is >= the author's account creation and <= creation + 30 days. Each row links a question to its author and question creation time.

questions_with_valid_creation.name: questions_with_valid_creation
questions_with_valid_creation.body_sql:
SELECT
  EXTRACT(DAYOFWEEK FROM creation_date) AS question_id,
  creation_date AS question_creation_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
WHERE
  creation_date IS NOT NULL
questions_with_valid_creation.description: All question posts that have a non-null creation_date; keep question id and creation timestamp (no aggregation).

earliest_answer_per_question.name: earliest_answer_per_question
earliest_answer_per_question.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(parent_id AS INT64) AS question_id,
  MIN(creation_date) AS earliest_answer_creation_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
WHERE
  post_type_id = 2
GROUP BY
  parent_id
earliest_answer_per_question.description: For each question, compute the earliest (minimum) answer creation timestamp. Questions with no answers are not present in this relation (they will be treated downstream as having no earliest answer).

questions_with_response_timing.name: questions_with_response_timing
questions_with_response_timing.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS question_id,
  q.creation_date AS question_creation_date,
  FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%A', q.creation_date) AS day_of_week,
  ea.earliest_answer_creation_date AS earliest_answer_creation_date,
  CASE
    WHEN ea.earliest_answer_creation_date IS NULL THEN FALSE
    WHEN TIMESTAMP_DIFF(ea.earliest_answer_creation_date, q.creation_date, SECOND) BETWEEN 0 AND 3600 THEN TRUE
    ELSE FALSE
  END AS answered_within_1_hour_flag
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` q
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    parent_id AS question_id,
    MIN(creation_date) AS earliest_answer_creation_date
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
  WHERE
    parent_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY
    parent_id
) ea
ON q.id = SAFE_CAST(ea.question_id AS INT64)
questions_with_response_timing.description: Join questions to their earliest answer timestamp (if any) and compute a flag indicating whether the earliest answer exists and occurs within 0 to 3600 seconds after the question creation; also derive day_of_week from the question creation timestamp. One row per question.

answers_posts.name: answers_posts
answers_posts.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(id AS INT64) AS post_id,
  owner_user_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.stackoverflow_posts`
WHERE
  post_type_id = 2
answers_posts.description: All posts that are answers (exclude questions); keep the post id, owner/user id, and any fields needed to associate with users.

eligible_users.name: eligible_users
eligible_users.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS user_id,
  display_name
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users`
WHERE
  reputation > 10
eligible_users.description: Users who meet the reputation filter (reputation greater than 10); keep user id and display name for later join.

answer_counts_per_user.name: answer_counts_per_user
answer_counts_per_user.body_sql:
SELECT
  owner_user_id,
  COUNT(1) AS answer_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
WHERE
  owner_user_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  owner_user_id
answer_counts_per_user.description: Count the number of answer posts per user by grouping the answers_posts relation by owner/user id. This produces one row per user with their answer_count.

eligible_users_answer_counts.name: eligible_users_answer_counts
eligible_users_answer_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.id AS user_id,
  u.display_name AS display_name,
  COALESCE(a.answer_count, 0) AS answer_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users` AS u
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    owner_user_id AS user_id,
    COUNT(1) AS answer_count
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
  WHERE
    owner_user_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY
    owner_user_id
) AS a
ON u.id = a.user_id
WHERE
  u.reputation > 10
eligible_users_answer_counts.description: Join the per-user answer counts to the eligible users to attach display_name to each user's answer_count. This relation is one row per user who has reputation > 10 and may include users with zero counts if desired (but typically only users present in answer_counts_per_user will appear).

questions_python2_cohort.name: questions_python2_cohort
questions_python2_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS question_id,
  q.title AS title,
  q.body AS body,
  q.tags AS tags,
  q.creation_date AS creation_date
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
WHERE
  -- only questions (post_type_id = 1) and not deleted (owner_user_id IS NOT NULL or other deletion indicators absent)
  q.post_type_id = 1
  AND q.id IS NOT NULL
  -- include if tags indicate Python 2 (tag string contains 'python-2' or 'python2' or 'py2')
  AND (
    LOWER(q.tags) LIKE '%python-2%'
    OR LOWER(q.tags) LIKE '%python2%'
    OR LOWER(q.tags) LIKE '%py2%'
    -- or if a language_tag column existed with 'python-2' (lifted out of view per instructions; not referenced here)
  )
  -- exclude any that mention Python 3 variants in title, body, or tags (case-insensitive)
  AND NOT (
    REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(IFNULL(q.title, '')), r'python[\s-]*3')
    OR REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(IFNULL(q.title, '')), r'python3')
    OR REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(IFNULL(q.title, '')), r'\bpy3\b')
    OR REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(IFNULL(q.title, '')), r'python-3')
    OR REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(IFNULL(q.body, '')), r'python[\s-]*3')
    OR REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(IFNULL(q.body, '')), r'python3')
    OR REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(IFNULL(q.body, '')), r'\bpy3\b')
    OR REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(IFNULL(q.body, '')), r'python-3')
    OR LOWER(IFNULL(q.tags, '')) LIKE '%python-3%'
    OR LOWER(IFNULL(q.tags, '')) LIKE '%python3%'
    OR LOWER(IFNULL(q.tags, '')) LIKE '%py3%'
  )
questions_python2_cohort.description: Select non-deleted posts that are questions and that are about Python 2: include posts whose tags indicate Python 2 or have a language_tag = 'python-2', and exclude any question whose title, body, or tags mention Python 3 variants (case-insensitive matches for 'python 3', 'python3', 'py3', 'python-3') or that have Python 3 tags. Keep only non-deleted questions.

answers_to_questions.name: answers_to_questions
answers_to_questions.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(a.id AS INT64) AS answer_id,
  CAST(a.parent_id AS INT64) AS parent_question_id,
  -- treat posts with NULL title and NULL body as deleted (since answers typically have body). 
  -- Lift literal: consider a post deleted if body IS NULL OR TRIM(body) = ''
  (CASE WHEN a.body IS NULL OR TRIM(a.body) = '' THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END) AS is_deleted,
  a.creation_date AS creation_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` AS a
WHERE
  -- keep only answers that have a parent question id
  a.parent_id IS NOT NULL
  -- ensure this row represents an answer post_type_id = 2 in the canonical posts table;
  -- posts_answers doesn't include post_type_id consistently, so we also require parent_id > 0
  AND a.parent_id > 0
  -- exclude rows that are clearly deleted by having both title and body NULL and no owner (conservative)
  -- (This filter is optional; we still carry is_deleted flag for downstream use.)
answers_to_questions.description: Select non-deleted posts that are answers and are linked to a parent question. Keep one row per answer with its parent question id.

answer_counts_per_question.name: answer_counts_per_question
answer_counts_per_question.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS question_id,
  COUNT(a.id) AS answer_count,
  q.title AS title
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` AS a
ON
  a.parent_id = q.id
  AND a.creation_date IS NOT NULL  -- treat presence as not-deleted indicator
WHERE
  -- Python 2 cohort: questions tagged with 'python-2.7' or 'python-2' (tags stored like '<tag1><tag2>')
  (REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(COALESCE(q.tags, '')), r'<python-2(\.7)?>') OR REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(COALESCE(q.tags, '')), r'<python-2\.7>'))
GROUP BY
  q.id, q.title
answer_counts_per_question.description: For the cohort of Python 2 questions, count the number of non-deleted answers linked to each question. Produce one row per question with its answer_count and include question metadata to allow returning an example question row.

answers_jan2016_sel.name: answers_jan2016_sel
answers_jan2016_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS answer_id,
  creation_date AS answer_creation_date,
  score AS answer_score,
  comment_count AS answer_comment_count,
  owner_user_id AS answer_owner_user_id,
  SAFE_CAST(accepted_answer_id IS NOT NULL AS BOOL) AS answer_is_accepted_flag
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
WHERE
  id IS NOT NULL
  AND owner_user_id IS NOT NULL
  AND creation_date >= TIMESTAMP("2016-01-01")
  AND creation_date < TIMESTAMP("2016-02-01")
answers_jan2016_sel.description: Select answers whose creation datetime is in January 2016 and that have non-null ids and author references; keep columns needed about the answer (id, creation_date, score, comment_count, owner_user_id, is_accepted_flag if present).

questions_jan2016_sel.name: questions_jan2016_sel
questions_jan2016_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS question_id,
  creation_date AS question_creation_date,
  score AS question_score,
  answer_count AS question_answer_count,
  view_count AS question_view_count,
  comment_count AS question_comment_count,
  accepted_answer_id AS question_accepted_answer_id,
  owner_user_id AS question_owner_user_id,
  -- return tags as a STRING (original pipe-delimited tags field)
  tags AS question_tags
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
WHERE
  -- January 2016: include all timestamps from 2016-01-01 (inclusive) to 2016-02-01 (exclusive)
  creation_date >= TIMESTAMP("2016-01-01") AND creation_date < TIMESTAMP("2016-02-01")
questions_jan2016_sel.description: Select questions created in January 2016 with their metadata and tags, including question id, creation_date, score, answer_count, view_count, comment_count, accepted_answer_id, owner_user_id, and the full tag set for each question (as a single field or normalized list).

questions_with_js_and_security_tags_filt.name: questions_with_js_and_security_tags_filter
questions_with_js_and_security_tags_filt.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS question_id,
  tags AS question_tags,
  score AS question_score,
  answer_count AS question_answer_count,
  view_count AS question_view_count,
  comment_count AS question_comment_count,
  accepted_answer_id AS question_accepted_answer_id,
  owner_user_id AS question_owner_user_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
WHERE
  -- January 2016 calendar month filter (lifted literal)
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM creation_date) = 2016
  AND EXTRACT(MONTH FROM creation_date) = 1
  -- must include 'javascript' as one of the tag tokens (tags are stored as e.g. '<tag1><tag2>')
  AND REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(tags), r'<javascript>')
  -- must include at least one security-related token (case-insensitive)
  AND REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(tags), r'<(xss|cross-site|exploit|cybersecurity)>')
questions_with_js_and_security_tags_filt.description: Filter the January-2016 questions to those whose tags include 'javascript' and at least one tag token matching 'xss', 'cross-site', 'exploit', or 'cybersecurity' (case-insensitive).

questions_2022_raw.name: questions_2022_raw
questions_2022_raw.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS question_id,
  creation_date,
  tags
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
WHERE
  post_type_id = 1
  AND creation_date IS NOT NULL
  AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM creation_date) = 2022
questions_2022_raw.description: Select all posts that are questions with a non-null creation date occurring in 2022 (inclusive). Keep the question id, creation date, and tag container as stored.

questions_2022_normalized.name: questions_2022_normalized
questions_2022_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS question_id,
  FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m', q.creation_date) AS year_month,
  tag AS tag_token
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q,
  UNNEST(
    -- split tags like '<tag1><tag2>' into array of tag strings without angle brackets
    CASE
      WHEN q.tags IS NULL OR q.tags = '' THEN []
      ELSE REGEXP_EXTRACT_ALL(q.tags, r'<([^>]+)>')
    END
  ) AS tag
questions_2022_normalized.description: Normalize the raw question rows to extract the year-month bucket (e.g. '2022-01') and produce a normalized representation of tags suitable for testing membership (e.g., an array or separated tokens). Do not apply the 'python' literal here.

questions_monthly_counts.name: questions_monthly_counts
questions_monthly_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  FORMAT_TIMESTAMP("%Y-%m", TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(creation_date, MONTH)) AS year_month,
  SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(SPLIT(REGEXP_REPLACE(tags, r"[<>]", ""), '><')) AS tag_token
    WHERE LOWER(tag_token) = 'python'
  ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS python_question_count,
  COUNT(1) AS total_question_count
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
GROUP BY year_month
ORDER BY year_month
questions_monthly_counts.description: Compute per-month aggregates: total number of questions in each year_month, and number of questions that have at least one tag_token equal to 'python'. This uses the normalized tag tokens to determine membership, but the literal 'python' filter is applied here as part of counting.

monthly_proportions.name: monthly_proportions
monthly_proportions.body_sql:
SELECT
  FORMAT_TIMESTAMP("%Y-%m", TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(creation_date, MONTH)) AS year_month,
  SUM(CASE WHEN REGEXP_CONTAINS(tags, r"(?i)\bpython\b") THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS python_question_count,
  COUNT(*) AS total_question_count,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(CASE WHEN REGEXP_CONTAINS(tags, r"(?i)\bpython\b") THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), COUNT(*)) AS proportion
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
WHERE
  creation_date >= TIMESTAMP("2022-01-01")
  AND creation_date < TIMESTAMP("2023-01-01")
GROUP BY
  year_month
ORDER BY
  year_month ASC
monthly_proportions.description: Compute the proportion for each month by dividing python_question_count by total_question_count and produce the final output rows for every month in 2022 (ordered ascending). Include month identifier, counts, and proportion.

questions_base_cohort.name: questions_base_cohort
questions_base_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(p.id AS INT64) AS question_id,
  COALESCE(p.title, '') AS title,
  COALESCE(p.body, '') AS body,
  p.view_count,
  p.score,
  p.creation_date,
  -- split tags string like "<tag1><tag2>" into an array of tag names; if NULL yield empty array
  CASE
    WHEN p.tags IS NULL OR p.tags = '' THEN []
    ELSE REGEXP_EXTRACT_ALL(p.tags, r'<([^>]+)>')
  END AS tags
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS p
WHERE
  -- lightweight canonicalization: ensure it's a question with an id and creation_date
  p.id IS NOT NULL
  AND p.creation_date IS NOT NULL
questions_base_cohort.description: Select the base set of question rows that include any of the target tags, retaining id, title, body, view_count, score, creation_date and the question's tags (as a set or array). This relation applies only lightweight canonicalization (e.g., ensure text fields and tags are available) but does not apply the 'how' or exclusion filters yet.

questions_text_filters.name: questions_text_filters
questions_text_filters.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS question_id,
  title,
  body,
  view_count,
  score,
  creation_date,
  tags
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
WHERE (
  -- include if title OR body contains 'how' (case-insensitive)
  (LOWER(IFNULL(title, "")) LIKE '%how%')
  OR
  (LOWER(IFNULL(body, "")) LIKE '%how%')
)
AND (
  -- exclude if title OR body contains any of the exclusion keywords (case-insensitive)
  NOT (
    LOWER(IFNULL(title, "")) LIKE '%fail%'
    OR LOWER(IFNULL(body, "")) LIKE '%fail%'
    OR LOWER(IFNULL(title, "")) LIKE '%problem%'
    OR LOWER(IFNULL(body, "")) LIKE '%problem%'
    OR LOWER(IFNULL(title, "")) LIKE '%error%'
    OR LOWER(IFNULL(body, "")) LIKE '%error%'
    OR LOWER(IFNULL(title, "")) LIKE '%wrong%'
    OR LOWER(IFNULL(body, "")) LIKE '%wrong%'
    OR LOWER(IFNULL(title, "")) LIKE '%fix%'
    OR LOWER(IFNULL(body, "")) LIKE '%fix%'
    OR LOWER(IFNULL(title, "")) LIKE '%bug%'
    OR LOWER(IFNULL(body, "")) LIKE '%bug%'
    OR LOWER(IFNULL(title, "")) LIKE '%issue%'
    OR LOWER(IFNULL(body, "")) LIKE '%issue%'
    OR LOWER(IFNULL(title, "")) LIKE '%solve%'
    OR LOWER(IFNULL(body, "")) LIKE '%solve%'
    OR LOWER(IFNULL(title, "")) LIKE '%trouble%'
    OR LOWER(IFNULL(body, "")) LIKE '%trouble%'
  )
)
questions_text_filters.description: Filter the base cohort to rows where the title OR body contains the substring 'how' (case-insensitive) and where NEITHER the title nor the body contain any of the exclusion substrings ('fail','problem','error','wrong','fix','bug','issue','solve','trouble'), case-insensitive. Preserve all question-level columns for downstream use.

questions_tag_expansion.name: questions_tag_expansion
questions_tag_expansion.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS question_id,
  tag AS tag,
  q.title AS title,
  q.body AS body,
  q.view_count AS view_count,
  q.score AS score,
  q.creation_date AS creation_date
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q,
UNNEST(SPLIT(REGEXP_REPLACE(q.tags, r'[<>]', ' '))) AS tag
WHERE tag IN UNNEST([
  'android',
  'android-activity',
  'android-intent',
  'android-fragments',
  'android-studio',
  'android-layout',
  'android-recyclerview',
  'android-gradle',
  'android-emulator',
  'kotlin-android'
])
questions_tag_expansion.description: Expand each question's tags so there is one row per (question_id, tag) pairing for tags in the target set. This produces a row for each question-tag combination (only for tags from the provided Android-related list) so we can evaluate per-tag counts and per-tag top-k. Do not apply the per-tag 50-limit yet.

stack_overflow_questions_sel.name: stack_overflow_questions_sel
stack_overflow_questions_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(p.id AS INT64) AS question_id,
  p.title AS title,
  'stackoverflow' AS site,
  p.tags AS tags,
  p.view_count AS view_count,
  p.creation_date AS creation_date
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS p
WHERE p.post_type_id = 1
stack_overflow_questions_sel.description: Select StackOverflow questions within the dataset (rows representing individual questions), retaining relevant metadata needed for filtering and ranking: title, site/source, tags (as a list or raw string), view_count, and creation/posting identifiers.

android_tagged_questions_sel.name: android_tagged_questions_sel
android_tagged_questions_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS question_id,
  title,
  tags,
  view_count
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
WHERE (
  -- Android-related tags: android, android-studio, android-layout, android-fragments, android-intent
  REGEXP_CONTAINS(CONCAT(',', SAFE_CAST(tags AS STRING), ','), r',\s*(android|android-studio|android-layout|android-fragments|android-intent)\s*,')
)
android_tagged_questions_sel.description: Subset of questions that contain at least one of the Android-related tags from the provided set. This filters the question rows by tag membership but does not aggregate or rank.

how_questions_norm.name: how_questions_norm
how_questions_norm.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry key
  id AS question_id,

  -- canonicalize title casing: trim and collapse internal whitespace, then
  -- use INITCAP-like behavior by lowercasing then capitalize first letter of each word.
  -- BigQuery has INITCAP() so use that after normalizing whitespace.
  -- keep original punctuation.
  NULLIF(REGEXP_REPLACE(TRIM(title), r'\s+', ' '), '') AS raw_title,
  INITCAP(NULLIF(REGEXP_REPLACE(TRIM(title), r'\s+', ' '), '')) AS title,

  -- flag common 'how' / 'how to' question patterns (case-insensitive)
  -- Lift literals out of view: patterns are defined here as regexes.
  -- Matches when the title begins with:
  --   how
  --   how to
  --   how do/does/did/can/could/should/would/is/are/what's/how's ... common variants
  -- Also match titles that exactly equal "how" or "how to ...".
  -- Use word boundary and optional punctuation after 'how' or 'how to'.
  (
    REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(COALESCE(NULLIF(REGEXP_REPLACE(TRIM(title), r'\s+', ' '), ''), '')),
      r'^(how\b|how to\b|how do\b|how does\b|how did\b|how can\b|how could\b|how should\b|how would\b|how is\b|how are\b|how\'s\b|how-in\b|how-to\b)'
    )
  ) AS is_how_question

FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
how_questions_norm.description: Normalize and identify questions that are phrased as 'how' questions. Canonicalize title casing and produce a boolean flag indicating whether the title begins with or matches common how/how-to question patterns (case-insensitive).

android_how_questions_rank.name: android_how_questions_rank
android_how_questions_rank.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS question_id,
  q.title AS title,
  q.view_count AS view_count,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY q.view_count DESC) AS rank
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
WHERE LOWER(q.tags) LIKE '%<android>%'
  AND LOWER(q.title) LIKE 'how %'
android_how_questions_rank.description: Combine the Android-tagged subset with the how-question flag and rank the resulting questions by view_count in descending order to identify the top question. Keep one row per question with its rank position.

question_answer_scores.name: question_answer_scores
question_answer_scores.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.`id` AS question_id,
  a.`id` AS answer_id,
  a.`owner_user_id` AS answer_author_id,
  a.`score` AS answer_score,
  q.`owner_user_id` AS question_owner_id,
  CAST(COALESCE(q.`view_count`, 0) AS INT64) AS question_view_count
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` AS a
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
  ON a.`parent_id` = q.`id`
question_answer_scores.description: All answers joined to their parent question, including the answer author, answer score, and the question's view count; normalize null view counts to 0. One row per answer. (This relation provides the base facts about each answer and its question.)

question_level_aggregates.name: question_level_aggregates
question_level_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(parent_id AS INT64) AS question_id,
  SUM(COALESCE(score,0)) AS total_answer_score,
  ARRAY(
    SELECT AS STRUCT score, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY score) AS ties_at_score, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY score DESC) AS score_rank
    FROM UNNEST((
      SELECT ARRAY_AGG(a_struct ORDER BY score DESC, answer_id) FROM (
        SELECT
          COALESCE(score,0) AS score,
          CAST(id AS STRING) AS answer_id
        FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` a
        WHERE a.parent_id IS NOT NULL
          AND CAST(a.parent_id AS INT64) = CAST(parent_id AS INT64)
      ) a_struct
    )) 
  ) AS top_answer_thresholds
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
WHERE parent_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY parent_id
question_level_aggregates.description: Per-question aggregates computed from all answers: total sum of answer scores, and a sorted list or score ranks needed to identify top-three answers and ties. One row per question.

answer_association_flags.name: answer_association_flags
answer_association_flags.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS question_id,
  a.id AS answer_id,
  a.owner_user_id AS answer_author_id,
  -- whether answer author equals question owner
  CASE WHEN a.owner_user_id IS NOT NULL AND q.owner_user_id IS NOT NULL AND a.owner_user_id = q.owner_user_id THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS is_question_owner,
  -- accepted flag: compare answer id to question.accepted_answer_id
  CASE WHEN q.accepted_answer_id IS NOT NULL AND CAST(q.accepted_answer_id AS INT64) = a.id THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS is_accepted,
  -- score > 5
  CASE WHEN a.score IS NOT NULL AND a.score > 5 THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS score_gt_5,
  -- answer score > 20% of question total answer score (question total provided by question_answer_scores view should be joined;
  -- lift literal 0.20 out of view: keep threshold as 0.20 to be applied here)
  CASE
    WHEN qa.total_answer_score IS NOT NULL AND a.score IS NOT NULL AND qa.total_answer_score > 0 AND CAST(a.score AS FLOAT64) > 0.20 * CAST(qa.total_answer_score AS FLOAT64) THEN TRUE
    ELSE FALSE
  END AS score_gt_20pct,
  -- is in top3 by score allowing ties: determine rank cutoff where scores >= third highest score (ties included)
  CASE WHEN qas.third_highest_score IS NOT NULL AND a.score IS NOT NULL AND a.score >= qas.third_highest_score THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS is_top3_tie
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` a
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` q
ON
  a.parent_id = q.id
-- question-level aggregates: total answer score per question
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    parent_id AS question_id,
    SUM(score) AS total_answer_score
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
  GROUP BY parent_id
) qa
ON qa.question_id = q.id
-- question answer scores with third highest score per question (ties allowed by using NTH_VALUE or array offset)
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    question_id,
    -- compute the third highest distinct score; if fewer than 3 distinct scores, use the minimum score present (so threshold behaves as "top available")
    COALESCE((
      SELECT DISTINCT s FROM UNNEST(ARRAY(
        SELECT score FROM UNNEST(scores_arr) AS score ORDER BY score DESC
      )) AS s LIMIT 1 OFFSET 2
    ), (
      SELECT MIN(score) FROM UNNEST(scores_arr) AS score
    )) AS third_highest_score
  FROM (
    SELECT
      parent_id AS question_id,
      ARRAY_AGG(score ORDER BY score DESC) AS scores_arr
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
    GROUP BY parent_id
  )
) qas
ON qas.question_id = q.id
answer_association_flags.description: For each answer (one row per answer), compute boolean flags indicating whether that answer meets each association rule for its author for the parent question: is_accepted, score_gt_5, score_gt_20pct_of_question_total_and_pos, is_in_top3_by_score. Also include whether the answer author equals the question owner. Uses question_level_aggregates and question_answer_scores.

user_answers_before_date.name: user_answers_before_date
user_answers_before_date.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS answer_id,
  parent_id AS question_id,
  creation_date,
  owner_user_id
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
WHERE owner_user_id = @target_user_id
  AND creation_date < @cutoff_timestamp
  AND post_type_id = 2
user_answers_before_date.description: All answers authored by the target user and posted strictly before the cutoff date. Keep answer identifiers and link to the parent question and answer creation timestamp.

answer_vote_counts.name: answer_vote_counts
answer_vote_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  v.post_id AS answer_id,
  SUM(CASE WHEN v.vote_type_id = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS upvote_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN v.vote_type_id = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS accepted_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.votes` v
GROUP BY
  v.post_id
answer_vote_counts.description: For each answer, count votes of the relevant types: number of upvotes (vote_type_id = 2) and number of accepted votes (vote_type_id = 1). Do not filter by date or user here (filtering happens by joining to user_answers_before_date).

questions_2021_cohort.name: questions_2021_cohort
questions_2021_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(id AS INT64) AS question_id,
  creation_date AS question_creation_ts
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
WHERE
  post_type_id = 1
  AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM creation_date) = 2021
  -- No explicit deletion flag exists in this table; if one is added later, filter it out here.
questions_2021_cohort.description: Select all Stack Overflow posts that are questions created in the calendar year 2021, excluding deleted posts if a deletion flag exists. Keep question id and creation timestamp and any flags needed to identify question posts.

question_answer_within_1hr_flag.name: question_answer_within_1hr_flag
question_answer_within_1hr_flag.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS question_id,
  q.creation_date AS question_creation_ts,
  -- flag: 1 if there exists at least one answer whose creation_date is <= 60 minutes after question.creation_date
  IF(
    EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` a
      WHERE a.parent_id = q.id
        AND TIMESTAMP_DIFF(a.creation_date, q.creation_date, MINUTE) BETWEEN 0 AND 60
    ), 1, 0
  ) AS has_answer_within_1hr
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` q
WHERE
  -- 2021 cohort: questions created in calendar year 2021
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM q.creation_date) = 2021
question_answer_within_1hr_flag.description: For each question (from the 2021 cohort) join to answers and determine, per question, whether there exists at least one answer whose creation timestamp is within 1 hour (<= 60 minutes) after the question creation timestamp. Produce one row per question with a boolean/integer flag indicating presence of such an answer.

questions_filtered.name: questions_filtered
questions_filtered.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- key/id
  id AS question_id,
  -- body text and length
  body AS body,
  LENGTH(body) AS body_length,
  -- view and accepted answer
  view_count AS view_count,
  accepted_answer_id AS accepted_answer_id,
  -- asking user id
  owner_user_id AS owner_user_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
WHERE
  -- ensure these are questions (post_type_id = 1 per StackOverflow schema) and exclude zero views
  post_type_id = 1
  AND view_count IS NOT NULL
  AND view_count != 0
questions_filtered.description: All posts that are questions (exclude answers), with their id, body text, body length, view count, accepted_answer_id, and asking user id; exclude questions with view_count = 0 to avoid division-by-zero in later filters.

answers_per_question.name: answers_per_question
answers_per_question.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS answer_id,
  parent_id AS parent_question_id,
  score
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
WHERE
  post_type_id = 2
answers_per_question.description: All answers with their id, parent question id, and score; used to test existence of answers that meet the score/view_count ratio condition and to detect accepted answers by id match.

question_answer_flags.name: question_answer_flags
question_answer_flags.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS question_id,
  -- whether question has an accepted answer (true if accepted_answer_id is not null)
  SAFE_CAST(q.accepted_answer_id IS NOT NULL AS BOOL) AS has_accepted_answer,
  -- whether exists at least one answer for this question with (answer.score / question.view_count) > @ratio_threshold
  -- note: ratio_threshold is lifted out as a parameter; default usage should set it to 0.01
  EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` a
    WHERE a.parent_id = q.id
      AND q.view_count IS NOT NULL
      AND q.view_count > 0
      AND SAFE_DIVIDE(a.score, q.view_count) > @ratio_threshold
  ) AS has_high_ratio_answer,
  -- length of question body (NULL-safe)
  IFNULL(CHAR_LENGTH(q.body), 0) AS body_length,
  q.view_count AS view_count,
  q.owner_user_id AS owner_user_id
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` q
question_answer_flags.description: Per-question aggregated flags indicating whether the question has any accepted answer (boolean) and whether it has at least one answer whose score divided by the question's view_count is > 0.01. Also keep the question's body_length and view_count for later ranking.

question_with_asker_stats.name: question_with_asker_stats
question_with_asker_stats.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS question_id,
  LENGTH(q.body) AS body_length,
  q.owner_user_id AS owner_user_id,
  u.reputation AS owner_reputation,
  u.up_votes AS owner_up_votes,
  u.down_votes AS owner_down_votes,
  -- total badge count for the owner; 0 when no badges
  COALESCE(b.owner_badge_count, 0) AS owner_badge_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users` AS u
ON
  q.owner_user_id = u.id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    user_id,
    COUNT(1) AS owner_badge_count
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.badges`
  GROUP BY
    user_id
) AS b
ON
  q.owner_user_id = b.user_id
question_with_asker_stats.description: For each qualifying question (one row per question), attach the asking user's statistics: reputation, up_votes, down_votes, and total badge count; do not perform final qualifying/filtering by length or top-K here.
